answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal registry. A new agent posts a hashed identity commitment to the shared atlas of participants, bonded with a verifiable compute puzzle, and only after a full epoch may it reveal the preimage and earn reputation weight. Reveals are appended to one ordered thread of the ledger, so nobody can backdate an identity to look established. An attacker spawning raven-1 through raven-1000 must burn a thousand puzzles of hardware time, wait out a thousand delays, and still forfeits every bond once two of those identities are caught voting in lockstep.
